name: Initial Access Vectors
description: How ransomware actors most commonly gain a foothold in transportation/warehousing environments, shaped by the industry's mix of legacy OT, distributed fleet/warehouse sites, and often-thin IT security staffing relative to operational scale.

name: Extortion Tactics
description: The specific leverage mechanisms ransomware groups use against transportation/logistics targets, reflecting a broader industry shift toward data theft and multi-pronged pressure over pure encryption.

id: operational technology ot and physical safety adjacent risk
name: Operational technology (OT) and physical-safety-adjacent risk
description: Unlike pure back-office IT sectors, hospitality/entertainment venues integrate IT with physical operations, so a ransomware event can directly disrupt guest safety, access, and physical service delivery, not just data confidentiality.

id: third party and supply chain risk
name: Third-Party / Supply-Chain Risk
description: Because logistics networks are inherently interconnected, an attack on one node (a carrier, a software vendor, a port) propagates operational and reputational damage across partners and customers.

name: Insider & Workforce Risk
description: Distributed, high-turnover workforces (drivers, warehouse staff, seasonal labor) and thin security-awareness investment create human-factor exposure distinct from office-centric industries.

name: Regulatory, contractual and reputational exposure
description: Data-protection, payment-card, and consumer-protection obligations that shape breach costs and downstream liability specific to guest-data-heavy businesses.

name: Extortion & Impact Tactics
description: The mix of leverage attackers apply. In this sector the physical perishability and food-security angle amplifies pressure to pay quickly.

id: ot ics and physical process risk
name: OT / ICS & Physical-Process Risk
description: Operational-technology exposure specific to farms and food plants where cyber impact becomes physical and food-safety relevant.

id: supply chain and third party concentration risk
name: Supply-Chain & Third-Party Concentration Risk
description: The sector's consolidation and just-in-time structure mean one victim's outage propagates widely; conversely, victims are exposed through their many upstream vendors.

id: regulatory legal and food security exposure
name: Regulatory, Legal & Food-Security Exposure
description: Compliance and liability hazards triggered by an incident, heightened by critical-infrastructure designation and personal-data holdings.

id: insider workforce and operational maturity risk
name: Insider, Workforce & Operational-Maturity Risk
description: Human and organizational weaknesses characteristic of the sector.

id: ot iot and jobsite facilities technology risk
name: OT, IoT and Jobsite/Facilities Technology Risk
description: Physical and operational-technology exposure distinct to construction and post-construction facilities management, generally less targeted today than pure-IT systems but a growing concern.

name: Regulatory & Legal Exposure
description: Telecom's status as a heavily regulated, often critical-infrastructure-designated sector amplifies post-incident financial and legal consequences beyond the ransom/attack itself.

name: Business Interruption / Project Delay Risk
description: How ransomware translates into operational and financial disruption specific to project-based construction work.

id: initial access via open and federated campus environments
name: Initial Access via Open and Federated Campus Environments
description: Education networks are architecturally adversarial to containment. Universities operate deliberately open networks supporting public research collaboration, guest access, self-managed student devices and thousands of transient accounts per year, while K-12 districts run flat networks with minimal segmentation and small IT teams. Sophos found exploited vulnerabilities to be the single largest root cause in higher education (35% of attacks) and phishing the leading cause in lower education (22%), reflecting the two different failure modes. Verizon DBIR data has repeatedly placed social engineering and system intrusion as the dominant education breach patterns.

id: extortion leverage from minors and student data
name: Extortion Leverage from Minors' and Student Data
description: Education is uniquely coercible because the hostage data belongs largely to children. Actors have moved from encryption-first to exfiltration-led extortion and apply pressure through channels unavailable in other sectors: publishing psychological evaluations, special-education records and abuse reports, and contacting students and parents directly. In the LAUSD and Minneapolis cases the leaked corpora included student psychological assessments, and in Minneapolis campus security blueprints - creating physical-safety as well as privacy harm. Sophos recorded extortion-only (no encryption) attacks rising in both education strata.

id: third party and edtech vendor concentration risk
name: Third-Party and Edtech Vendor Concentration Risk
description: The single most severe systemic hazard in the sector. A handful of SIS, LMS and assessment platforms serve most of the addressable market, so one vendor intrusion becomes a correlated loss across thousands of insureds simultaneously. PowerSchool (Dec 2024) reached a claimed 62.4 million students and 9.5 million teachers across approximately 6,505 districts from one compromised credential; Instructure/Canvas (May 2026) was claimed to affect 275 million users across roughly 9,000 institutions. Verizon's 2026 DBIR reported third-party involvement in 48% of breaches with supply-chain breaches up 60%. For a cyber-insurance portfolio this is the dominant aggregation exposure in the education book.

name: Insider and Student-Originated Threat
description: Education is the rare sector in which a substantial share of the resident population is both technically capable and directly motivated to attack the institution's systems - for grade alteration, exam access or reputational reasons - while holding legitimate network credentials. The PowerSchool intrusion was ultimately attributed by the US DOJ to a 19-year-old university student, who pleaded guilty. Insider events blur the ransomware/fraud boundary and complicate coverage triggers.

name: Regulatory, Notification and Litigation Exposure
description: Education carries a dense, overlapping and unusually child-focused compliance regime, so a single ransomware event generates parallel regulatory tracks. FERPA and COPPA apply federally in the US, layered with state student-privacy statutes and state breach laws; UK and EU institutions face UK GDPR/GDPR and ICO scrutiny; universities holding clinical or research-health data additionally trigger HIPAA. Notification is frequently slow - Minneapolis took seven months to notify 105,617 people, and the University of Hawai'i Cancer Center's delay in notifying study participants drew specific criticism - which compounds regulatory and class-action risk.

id: operational disruption of instruction and institutional continuity
name: Operational Disruption of Instruction and Institutional Continuity
description: Unlike most commercial insureds, schools cannot fail over to a degraded manual mode: an encrypted district frequently closes entirely. Highline Public Schools shut all 34 schools for three days; the British Library's core services were disrupted for months. Comparitech measured an average of 10.7 days of downtime per education incident, peaking at 12.6 days in 2023. Lost instructional days carry statutory make-up obligations, transport and meal-programme knock-ons, and in higher education can delay terms, research grants and graduation.

id: underfunded security posture and recovery capability
name: Underfunded Security Posture and Recovery Capability
description: The sector's loss severity is driven less by attacker sophistication than by chronic under-resourcing. Sophos found lack of expertise and limited incident-response capacity cited by 42% each in lower education, and 49% of higher education institutions citing unknown security gaps. Backup reliability has degraded: recovery from backups fell to 59% in lower education and 47% in higher education. Public institutions face procurement cycles, capital-budget constraints and elected-board approval that slow both hardening and response.

id: ot vs it risk cyber physical
name: OT vs IT Risk (Cyber-Physical)
description: The defining hazard of this sector: the interface between enterprise IT and operational technology (ICS/SCADA/DCS) controlling physical energy flows. IT-only ransomware routinely forces OT shutdowns, and OT-capable malware threatens physical damage.

name: Regulatory, Legal & Reputational Exposure
description: Energy is heavily regulated as critical infrastructure; incidents trigger mandatory reporting, sanctions-screening on ransom payment, and public/political scrutiny.

name: Systemic and Market-Contagion Risk
description: A hazard category distinct to this industry: ransomware against a single financial institution or vendor can cascade into broader market or payment-system disruption well beyond the immediate victim.

name: Operational/Business-Continuity Risk
description: How ransomware-driven downtime specifically manifests in financial and insurance operations, which are unusually time-sensitive and trust-dependent.

id: ot medical device and clinical operations risk
name: OT / Medical-Device and Clinical-Operations Risk
description: Unlike most sectors, ransomware in healthcare directly threatens physical patient safety through disruption of connected medical equipment and clinical workflows, not just IT/data confidentiality.

id: supply chain and downstream cascade risk
name: Supply-Chain and Downstream Cascade Risk
description: The signature hazard of the IT industry: because these firms are technology suppliers, a single compromise propagates to their entire customer base, creating catastrophic aggregation/accumulation risk for insurers.

id: intellectual property and source code theft
name: Intellectual Property and Source Code Theft
description: IT firms hold uniquely high-value technical IP whose theft is itself the extortion leverage, independent of encryption.

id: third party vendor and concentration risk
name: Third-Party, Vendor and Concentration Risk
description: Dependence on shared infrastructure and a dense web of subprocessors amplifies both the likelihood and blast radius of incidents.

id: insider identity and privileged access risk
name: Insider, Identity and Privileged-Access Risk
description: IT staff hold the keys to both their own and customers' environments, making identity compromise and privileged-access abuse especially damaging.

id: infrastructure and availability risk it data center
name: Infrastructure and Availability Risk (IT/Data-Center)
description: For the IT sector the critical 'operational technology' is the data center, network and cloud fabric; loss of availability is the primary business-interruption driver rather than physical production lines.

name: OT vs. IT Risk Differentiation
description: Manufacturing's unique bifurcated risk profile — attacks can remain IT-contained (data theft) or cross into OT (halting physical production), with dramatically different loss profiles.

id: supply chain and business interruption risk
name: Supply Chain and Business Interruption Risk
description: Because manufacturers sit inside just-in-time, tightly coupled supply chains, a single-site ransomware event can cascade into contingent business interruption for downstream customers and upstream suppliers well beyond the insured's own balance sheet.

id: third party and vendor msp risk
name: Third-Party and Vendor/MSP Risk
description: Reliance on external integrators, MSPs, and cloud/SaaS platforms for both IT and OT management creates an attack surface outside the manufacturer's direct control.

name: Regulatory, Legal, and Notification Exposure
description: Post-incident compliance and liability obligations that shape the insurable loss beyond the ransom/recovery cost itself, particularly where employee, customer, or government-ID data is exposed.

name: Confidentiality / privileged-data risk
description: Professional/technical services firms hold sensitive third-party information whose exposure carries outsized legal and reputational consequences.

name: Operational / logistics disruption
description: Hazards specific to wholesale trade and logistics operations where system downtime directly halts physical goods movement.

name: Insider and credential risk
description: Distributed, high-turnover workforces common to staffing, real estate brokerage, and professional-services firms increase credential and insider exposure.

id: service disruption availability risk mission critical public services
name: Service-Disruption / Availability Risk (mission-critical public services)
description: Government-specific operational hazards where downtime directly harms public safety and essential service delivery, not just revenue.

name: OT / Critical-Infrastructure Adjacency
description: Where government IT connects to operational technology and public-safety infrastructure, expanding blast radius beyond data loss.

id: third party supply chain and aggregation risk
name: Third-Party, Supply-Chain & Aggregation Risk
description: Systemic exposure unique to government's shared and outsourced service model, where one compromise cascades across many jurisdictions.

name: Regulatory, Legal & Political Exposure
description: Post-incident obligations and accountability pressures distinctive to public bodies answerable to citizens and oversight bodies.

name: Threat-Actor Landscape
description: The specific ransomware ecosystems and actor types repeatedly hitting government, blending crime and, at national level, state interests.

name: Operational and Store-Network Disruption
description: Because retail margins depend on continuous inventory flow and point-of-sale availability, ransomware's operational-availability impact (not just data loss) is often the largest cost driver in this industry.

name: Regulatory, Legal, and Disclosure Exposure
description: Consumer-facing businesses face a dense, overlapping set of breach-notification, payment-card, and consumer-protection obligations that amplify post-incident cost and litigation risk beyond the direct technical recovery.

name: Reputational and Customer-Trust Risk
description: Because purchase decisions in retail and consumer services are discretionary and brand-sensitive, publicized ransomware incidents translate directly into measurable revenue and market-value loss, distinct from the direct IR/ransom cost.

id: core network availability disruption ot equivalent risk
name: Core Network / Availability Disruption ('OT-equivalent' risk)
description: Telecom's version of OT/ICS risk - attacks that threaten service availability at national or regional scale rather than just confidentiality.

name: Insider & Credential-Based Risk
description: Human-layer risk distinct from bulk phishing - individual employee/admin compromise with outsized consequences given telecom's centralized subscriber-identity role.

name: OT vs IT Risk
description: Transportation/warehousing uniquely blends conventional IT (billing, CRM, EDI) with operational technology controlling physical movement of goods — an intrusion in either domain can halt the other.

name: Regulatory & Financial Exposure
description: Transportation's critical-infrastructure designation and highly interconnected, low-margin business model amplify the downstream consequences of an incident beyond the direct IT-remediation cost.
